description: §17.1.2 — `if=` on a block-form `<match>` gates the DISPATCHED ARM OUTPUT: while the condition is false no arm is dispatched at all. `@shown` seeds false and nothing flips it, so #arm-loading and #arm-ready must both be count 0 and the `data-scrml-match-mount` slot must not exist either. Before this widening the attribute generated ZERO code and the mount slot dispatched normally. The subject cell is driven anyway (#ready flips @phase to .Ready) to show that the gate withholds the DISPATCH, not the subject: @phase must still read Ready. `<match>` carries no independent state, so the §17.1.2.1 render-vs-lifecycle distinction is vacuous here — the whole claim is the absence.
rationale: §17.1.2's table admits `if=` on `<match>` (§18.0.1) and scopes §17.1 semantics to "the dispatched arm output". §17.1: "When `expr` evaluates to false, the element is NOT rendered. It does not exist in the DOM." §17.2 draws the contrast — "`show=` hides, `if=` removes" — so a `display:none` lowering would not satisfy this case; the count-0 assertions are on DOM existence, and the arm markup legitimately remains in the emitted BYTES inside the inert `<template>` the §17.1 lowering produces.
